_meta.asymmetry_caveat: Because the harness short-circuits on the FIRST env (sci2024) passing, we can only reconstruct 'steps that differ between sci2024-alone and OR(sci2024,cp312)' -- i.e. rescues in the sci2024->cp312 direction. Empirically, in every rescue we DID observe, cp312 is the environment that passes and sci2024 is the one that fails (0 cases of the reverse), consistent with the two categories of root cause identified below.

notes: Deviation from the task's stated expectation ('2-3 steps per model, all library-API drift like scipy simps->simpson removal'): ACTUAL counts are 7-9 rescued steps per model (gpt-5.5=8, gemini-flash=7, opus-4.8=9, glm-5.2=8), i.e. roughly 3x the expected magnitude, and NEITHER dominant root cause is the anticipated scipy.integrate.simps/cumtrapz-style deprecation. The two confirmed root causes are: (1) matplotlib/mpl_toolkits is simply NOT INSTALLED in the sci2024 conda env (a packaging gap, not an API-version issue) and poisons every step of problem 80 (Anderson_thermostat) via its shared required_dependencies import -- this alone accounts for 6-7 of every model's rescued steps; (2) numpy 1.26.4's np.linalg.{svd,eigvalsh} explicitly raises `TypeError: array type complex256 is unsupported in linalg` for the complex256/longdouble-precision arrays that scipy 1.13.1's scipy.linalg.sqrtm produces for near-singular quantum-state density matrices in problem 65 (GHZ_protocol_fidelity) -- this accounts for 1-2 rescued steps per model. This IS still a form of 'library version drift' in spirit (a numpy/scipy version pairing that rejects a dtype/import the newer pairing accepts), but it is a different, narrower, and more environment-specific pair of bugs than the assumed scipy function-renaming pattern -- flagging this prominently per instructions.

opus-4.8's 60.5 (Widom_particle_insertion) is the ONE rescued step not explained by either of the two shared root causes above. Its cache verdict (2024:false / 2025:true) is 100% certain (cross-checked identically on sichuan2 and the local mirror), but capturing the actual stderr required literally re-executing this specific heavy Monte-Carlo cumulative script, which did not finish within the time available for this report (still running past 700s under sci2024 and 450s under cp312 -- the original harness allows up to 1800s per step, so this is plausible and not itself anomalous). Do not assume this is API-drift; static inspection of the code (wrap/E_i/Widom_insertion/init_system/MC) shows nothing that looks version-specific. If precision matters for the paper, this needs a follow-up dedicated (background, unhurried) reproduction.

Methodological caveat (short-circuit asymmetry): run_deepseek_eval.py's score_step tries env '2024' (sci2024) FIRST and stops as soon as one env passes. Consequently the cache can only reveal the sci2024-vs-OR rescue direction; it structurally cannot reveal whether any of the 234-272 steps that passed on the first (sci2024) try would also have passed under cp312 alone, because cp312 was never invoked for those steps. Empirically, in every case where BOTH envs were tried, cp312 was the one that passed when sci2024 failed -- zero instances of the reverse were observed -- consistent with sci2024 being the older/more restrictive environment for these two bug classes.
